notes: Compressed long-session proxy for GitHub Copilot CLI: 4 plain-prompt turns in ONE interactive session, with turn 3 additionally running an --allow-all-approved bash `echo gamma` so the run satisfies the scenario's 'includes at least one tool call'. Spec asserts the per-turn ready→working→ready arc with NO flicker WITHIN a turn, no stuck state, and final state ready. WHY within-turn no-flicker is STRUCTURAL here (parser.go + state_classifier.go): assistant.turn_end is the ONLY event mapped to turn_done, so there is exactly one settle per turn and it is READ, not inferred from a quiet tail (contrast gemini-cli, whose text-only assistant message IS the settle and can therefore fire early); parseAssistantMessage always emits assistant_message and never settles; tool.execution_start/tool.execution_complete pair on toolCallId so a result CLOSES the open call rather than gating it, and a failed call sets only IsError, which no classifier rule reads. The classifier ladder has no rule keyed on assistant_message or function_call_output — ready comes only from agent_done (needs turn_done) or user_interrupt (needs LastWasUserInterrupt/LastWasToolDenial, neither of which the copilot parser ever sets). waiting is reachable for copilot ONLY via the transcript-tier permission rule fed by permission.requested, and --allow-all means none is ever written, so the no-waiting invariants are structural. PRESESSION BIRTH: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle mints a proc-<PID> row first (1s poll) and the real dir-keyed session id arrives later — modelled as two phases with every later phase anchored same_session_as session_birth, matching the committed basic-turn and auto-executed-tool-call cells. The t3_working dwell pins the within-turn invariant on the tool-calling turn, the one most likely to flicker. PROVISIONAL on emission: a code read proves the daemon CANNOT settle mid-turn, but cannot prove copilot never writes a second assistant.turn_end mid-turn nor that turns don't collapse into one tailer pass — only the live recording settles that, which is why a credit-free BYOK-against-a-mock recording was rejected for this cell (a canned mock would prove the mock doesn't flicker, not that copilot doesn't). OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map (session.usage_checkpoint carries no token counts at all — only shutdown does), so both are asserted non-zero. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn, so a 4-turn run can legitimately span two models.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
Real <session-id> session reconciles under a DIFFERENT session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, born ready
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
Turn 1 ends; assistant.turn_end settles working → ready; the session never entered waiting
Turn 2 prompt drives ready → working (clean between-turn re-open)
Turn 3 prompt drives ready → working; this is the turn that runs the bash `echo gamma` tool call (scenario bullet: includes at least one tool call)

State stays continuously working across the tool-call cycle — the tool.execution_start/tool.execution_complete pair and the surrounding assistant.message fragments must NOT flicker the session to ready or waiting before assistant.turn_end (within-turn no-flicker, scenario bullet 1)
Turn 3 ends; assistant.turn_end settles working → ready after the post-tool reply; --allow-all means no permission.requested, so waiting was never entered
Final turn ends; working → ready. Session reaches ready and stays there (scenario bullets 3 & 4) — state was never stuck in any single state across the run
